Test for overdispersion: Poisson against negative binomial

Source: R/inference.R
overdispersion_test.Rd

Tests whether the negative binomial model fits better than the Poisson model, which is its limit as theta goes to infinity. The Poisson model is refitted (by IRLS, with the same covariates, offset and weights), and the likelihood-ratio statistic LR = 2 (loglik_NB - loglik_Poisson) is computed. Because the null value theta = Inf lies on the boundary of the parameter space, LR is referred to an equal mixture of a point mass at 0 and a chi-squared distribution with 1 degree of freedom, so the p-value is half the usual one: p = P(chisq(1) > LR) / 2. This is the test of pscl::odTest().

Usage

overdispersion_test(object, ...)

Arguments

object

An nbreg fit.

...

Not used (an error if supplied).

Value

An object of class htest with the statistic LR, the p.value, the estimate of theta, the null value theta = Inf, and a note (also shown in method) when one of the special cases applies.

Details

theta on its upper bound. The fit keeps theta below theta_max (1e8 by default), a computational bound, not the true limit. If the fit ended there:

  • if the NB log-likelihood equals the Poisson one (within 1e-6 * (|loglik| + 1)) and still rises toward the bound, the fit is at the Poisson limit: LR = 0 and p = 0.5, with a note;

  • otherwise the bound cuts off a real improvement: LR is reported at theta_max, but the p-value is NA, with an nbzinbreg_warning_theta asking for a larger theta_max.

theta on its lower bound. LR is then a lower bound for the true statistic, so the p-value is an upper bound. It is reported with a note and an nbzinbreg_warning_theta.

A negative statistic beyond rounding is impossible at the maxima. The NB model is then refitted from the Poisson estimates; if that beats the stored fit, the fit is not at its maximum and an nbzinbreg_error_fit is raised.

Errors and warnings

  • nbzinbreg_error_input: object is not an nbreg fit (for a zinbreg fit the zero-inflated Poisson comparison is not available), or unused arguments.

  • nbzinbreg_error_fit: the Poisson fit failed or did not converge, or the NB fit is not at its maximum.

  • nbzinbreg_warning_theta: theta on a bound (see above).

  • nbzinbreg_warning_convergence: the NB fit did not converge. The statistic is still reported, for diagnosis only, but the p-value is NA.

See also

anova.nbreg(), vuong_test()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("pscl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
  fit <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
  overdispersion_test(fit)
}
#> 
#> 	Likelihood-ratio test for overdispersion (Poisson against negative
#> 	binomial; boundary-corrected p-value)
#> 
#> data:  art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment
#> LR = 180.2, p-value < 2.2e-16
#> alternative hypothesis: true theta is less than Inf
#> sample estimates:
#>    theta 
#> 2.264388 
#>
